CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left ankle pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Stephanie Morales is a 36-year-old female presenting with left ankle pain after a fall two days ago. Patient slipped on ice and snow while walking to her car, causing her left ankle to twist on the lateral aspect. She fell down but was able to get up. The ankle became very sore with significant swelling and pain, making ambulation difficult. She has tried ibuprofen, ice, and elevation with some relief. Pain is localized to the outside of the ankle. Denies pain in the calf, lower leg, or knee. Denies bleeding.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports diabetes-related blood sugars have been stable with diet management and regular monitoring. Blood pressure well-controlled. Denies other symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Diabetes mellitus
2. Hypertension
3. Systolic ejection murmur (2/6, unchanged from prior)

MEDICATIONS
1. Metformin
2. Norvasc

ALLERGIES
None documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not documented

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neck: No bruits. Lungs: Clear. Heart: Normal rate and rhythm, 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (unchanged from prior). Abdomen: Benign. Left ankle: Tenderness over lateral malleolus and fifth metatarsal, swelling, redness, pain with valgus stressing. Normal sensation and normal pulses distally.

RESULTS
HbA1c 6.8 (prior). Blood pressure 120/70.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Left ankle sprain with concern for fifth metatarsal fracture. Order x-ray of left ankle. Place in air splint and provide crutches. Strict non-weightbearing until x-ray results reviewed. Naprosyn 500 mg PO BID for pain. Continue ice and elevation. If fracture present on x-ray, refer to orthopedics. If no fracture, remove splint and advance to partial weightbearing.

2. Diabetes mellitus - well-controlled. Continue metformin. Keep scheduled ophthalmology appointment. Order repeat HbA1c and baseline labs today.

3. Hypertension - well-controlled. Refill Norvasc today. Continue current management and monitoring.
